newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 7-Eleven store seeks IPO nod.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 7-Eleven store seeks IPO nod.

text.p: Philippine Seven Corp (PSC), the local licensee of the 7-Eleven chain of convenience stores, said on Monday it had filed a petition with the Securities Exchange Commission to undertake an initial public offering.
The company said in a statement it intends to offer to the public in May or June this year 61.8 to 72.9 million common shares, representing 27.10 percent to 30.4 percent of its capital.
The proposed offer price for the shares range from 8.24 to 9.72 pesos, equivalent to a price-earnings multiple of 16 to 18 times forecast 1997 earnings.
PSC chairman Vicente Paterno said the proceeds of the IPO will be used for store construction and expansion. It intends to double its number of stores to 200 by the end of 1998.

In the same statement, Philippine Seven Holdings Corp (PSHC), a holding company composed of the same shareholders as PSC, said it planned to issue 350 million pesos worth of warrants to domestic and foreign investors.
Each warrant will entitle the holder to purchase one common share of PSC held by PHSC at a strike price equivalent to the IPO price of PSC shares.

The warrants will enable foreign investors to participate in the offer because current laws prohibit foreign ownership in retailing. The opening of the retail trade to foreign investors, however, has been proposed in Congress.
The warrants are proposed to be offered at 8.30 to 9.80 pesos, the statement said.
BPI Capital Corp had been engaged to manage the IPO and the issuance of the warrants, the statement added.
